verifications.claim: SpaceX successfully launched a Falcon 9 rocket carrying 29 Starlink satellites from Cape Canaveral, Florida, on March 22, 2026, at 10:47 a.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket lifts off from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on the Starlink 10-62 mission on Sunday, March 22, 2026... Launch took place at 10:47 a.m. EDT (1447 UTC)... The Starlink 10-62 mission features 29 of SpaceX’s Starlink V2 Mini Optimized satellites'; R2: 'SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket... launch 29 Starlink satellites... Sunday, March 22... Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station'; R3: 'Liftoff of the Starlink 10-62 mission from pad 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station happened at 10:47 a.m. EDT (1447 UTC)'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references directly confirm the exact launch details, date, time, location, rocket, payload count, and success.

verifications.claim: The first-stage booster of the Falcon 9 rocket landed on a droneship in the Atlantic Ocean.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Nearly 8.5 minutes after liftoff, B1078 landed on the drone ship, ‘A Shortfall of Gravitas,’ positioned in the Atlantic Ocean.'
verifications.reasoning: R1 explicitly states the first-stage booster landing on a droneship in the Atlantic Ocean for this mission.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Starlink 10-62 mission'; R2: 'SpaceX Starlink 10-62'; R3: 'Starlink 10-62 mission'
verifications.reasoning: All three references directly name the mission as Starlink 10-62.

verifications.claim: The launch location was Space Launch Complex 40 (SLC-40) at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station'; R2: 'Location: Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station'; R3: 'pad 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station'
verifications.reasoning: References precisely match the launch site as SLC-40 (pad 40 / Launch Complex 40) at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station.

verifications.claim: NASA's Artemis II rocket is expected to launch between April 1st and April 6th, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Artemis 2 mission, which is currently set to launch no earlier than April 1, 2026'; R5: 'Officials hope for liftoff between April 1 and April 6... targeting April 1st as our first opportunity... six launch opportunities in April. So from April 1st to April 6th'
verifications.reasoning: R5 directly states the exact window April 1-6, 2026; R3 supports with no earlier than April 1.

verifications.claim: NASA's Artemis II rocket had a successful rollout to the launch pad on March 20, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'NASA's rollout of the Artemis II rocket complete after wind delay... Updated: 4:27 PM EDT Mar 20, 2026... rollout is complete after a wind delay overnight'; R3: 'The rollout of the 322-foot-tall rocket took fewer than 12 hours after first motion, which occurred at about 12:20 a.m. EDT (0420 UTC)'
verifications.reasoning: R5 confirms successful rollout completion on March 20, 2026, after delay; R3 describes the rollout process aligning with that date.
